top.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
top.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. top.title: Ben James Seizes Weekend Lead At World Wide Technology Championship
top.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Ben James took control of the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship on Friday night in Los Cabos. The rookie’s aggressive 64 (8-under) moved him to 129 (15-under) after 36 holes at El Cardonal at Diamante, a course designed by Tiger Woods. Darkness forced a suspension of play at 5:48 p.m. local time, leaving 12 golfers on the course to finish their rounds on Saturday morning. James now holds a one-shot lead heading into the weekend, according to Sportsnet.ca reporting from the field. During the second round, James made five straight birdies around the turn. He capped the round with a final birdie on the ninth hole. Since turning professional out of Virginia this summer, this performance represents his 14th round of 65 or lower across just 13 tournaments. This victory would secure a spot on the 2028 Championship Series under the new model and move the team into the top 50 in world rankings. Adapting to Professional Pressure James acknowledged the shift in scoring ability required at this level compared to his collegiate days. “It’s weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low,” James said. “But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that’s what you have to do. I’ve been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers.” “I’m doing everything right,” James said. “But for me, I’m just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand.” Malnati Chases Contention Peter Malnati sat tied for the lead until a critical error on the par-3 ninth hole. He fell short of the green and missed a 12-foot par putt, concluding his round of 64. The missed opportunity left him one shot behind James. “I work really hard on my game and I haven’t had tons to show for that lately,” Malnati said. “So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where … I don’t even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun.” Zac Blair shot a 68 to sit three shots behind the leader. Sudarshan Yellamaraju of Mississauga, Ont.James was six shots ahead, He is the top Canadian at 10 under. Ben Silverman of Thornhill, Ont., finished at 9 under, while Adam Svensson of Surrey, B.C., was at 7 under. Nick Taylor of Abbotsford, B.C., also made the cut at 5 under. Defending champion Ben Griffin and fellow North Carolina Tar Heel Ryan Gerard headline the field, with Griffin being one of six past champions competing in Cabo, per Central Oregon Daily . Cut Line and Schedule Saturday morning will see the 36-hole cut announced. Late Friday, 75 golfers were projected to make the cut at 5 under, although two players on the number still needed to finish their second rounds. A 72nd-minute strike from captain Martin Odegaard finally pierced a resilient five-man Hull defence. It was a tactical battle of attrition at the Emirates Stadium as Arsenal eventually wore down a remarkably disciplined Hull City side. The Gunners dominated 67 per cent of the ball and fired off 21 shots, yet they found clear-cut opportunities difficult to come by against the Tigers' low block. A controversial first-half VAR decision to deny Kai Havertz a penalty for offside added to the tension, leaving Mikel Arteta and the home crowd increasingly frustrated as the game remained goalless at the break. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 72nd minute through the persistent Martin Odegaard, who found the space to beat the impressive Konstantinos Tzolakis. top.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
top.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. top.title: Jared McCain rediscovers outside jumper in OKC's win over Grizzlies
top.description: On a pair of catch-and-shoot looks, Jared McCain rediscovered his groove. His undermanned squad quickly put up a double-digit lead. They can thank their en-fuego-style outside shooting for that. After a cold spell, the 22-year-old showed what the positive side of his shooting variance can look like. The Oklahoma City Thunder looked their best since Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) started with a 124-97 win over the Memphis Grizzlies . The butt-whooping was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B stage. McCain finished with 21 points on 9-of-14 shooting and five rebounds. He shot 3-of-8 from 3. He also had four steals and one block. Do you think McCain heard Bennett Stirtz's footsteps coming for his playing time? He's certainly played like somebody with a fire lit underneath his seat. Showing an inkling of confidence, the microwave scorer was hot throughout the night. Sure, the outside jumpers fell. But his scoring attack within the paint has also been a nice surprise so far. "Getting those transition shots where you got to guard Ajay, me or Shai, them driving to the basket is awesome for us," McCain said. "They make great decisions. For us, we just continue that. At halftime, we just kept our foot on the pedal." McCain had 12 points in the first quarter. He helped the Thunder get away from this one early. As Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gladly took a backseat after back-to-back 40-point nights, it was he and Ajay Mitchell who delivered OKC's first lethal punch to Memphis. The two absolutely demoralized the hot-shot, young, up-and-coming squad. This is what the best version of McCain looks like. When he's zoned in, he needs little time to drop points in a flurry. The Thunder have learned to play a team-friendly offensive style that lessens the burden on Gilgeous-Alexander. This is what it tangibly looks like. He made OKC's decision to start him look like an absolute genius move. "I think we're just playing together on a string. Defensively, we know what each other brings before and in the season, obviously," McCain said. "And then when people got hurt, we had to kinda figure it out. Now, we kinda know each other. We know certain things we like to do on the defensive end." This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Jared McCain rediscovers outside jumper in OKC's win over Grizzlies

top.description: A concerning update about Deshaun Watson emerged on Friday. It came amid the Cleveland Browns’ announcement that Shedeur Sanders will start for them in Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints. Watson suffered a concussion last Sunday during Cleveland’s 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The league takes these cases seriously and players need to pass a series of tests before they are cleared to return to action. The star quarterback has appeared and started in the first eight games of the season. He has 163-of-249 completions for 1,806 yards and seven touchdowns against three interceptions. Watson joined the Browns in March 2022 following a trade from the Houston Texans. He then signed a fully guaranteed, five-year, $230 million deal, making it the largest guaranteed contract in NFL history at the time. The former Clemson star entered the league in 2017 as the No. 17 overall pick. Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) after the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Huntington Bank Field. Worrying Deshaun Watson News Emerges on Friday Deshaun Watson returned to practice on Friday but remains in concussion protocol. He missed the sessions in the previous two games, with Sanders taking first team reps. The second-year quarterback has been named the QB1 for Sunday. ESPN’s Adam Schefter issued an update on Watson’s condition. “Deshaun Watson was checked for a concussion during the game, cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol during the game, and then shortly after the game reported symptoms to the team,” Schefter said. “And at that point, they knew he would end up in the concussion protocol. So (he) did not practice Wednesday and Thursday (but) was able to practice today. “(He) has not cleared the protocol, but there is at least a chance they could be active as a backup. top.title: Tom Brady Returns To Broadcast Patriots Game Sunday
top.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The legend walks back into Gillette Stadium, but not as the man who threw the passes, according to Sports Illustrated . Tom Brady will serve as a broadcaster for the first time on Sunday, calling the Patriots game against the Green Bay Packers. This marks a major shift for the seven-time Super Bowl champion, who has skipped calling his old team since joining FOX Sports in 2024. The network finally puts him in the booth for this matchup, ending a long dry spell of him avoiding New England on air. Brady told FOX’s Colin Cowherd that the moment feels heavy. This week, Brady told FOX’s Colin Cowherd, “It’ll certainly be emotional,” and he plans to focus on the team’s culture rather than his own past glory. The plan is to show fans how the program works right now. This approach fits a team that has moved past the dynasty years and is building something new under coach Mike Vrabel. Vrabel Keeps It Light Head coach Mike Vrabel took a different view when asked about his former teammate. He played eight years with Brady and won three Super Bowls together. Instead of getting emotional, Vrabel joked that he would handle their catch-up over a video call. He noted that he expects to see Brady in person soon at Rob Gronkowski’s Hall of Fame induction on Saturday. The banter shows a comfortable relationship between the two men. Vrabel knows the history, but he is focused on the present season. The Patriots are 5-3 and looking to build momentum after a win in Miami. Weather and Rivalry History The game faces a different kind of pressure from the sky. Apple Weather projects an 80% chance of rain for the area on Sunday. Most of the water is expected to fall before the game starts. By the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, the forecast calls for only a 20% chance of rain. Fans should bring a jacket as temperatures drop into the upper 40s by the end of the game. This matchup also carries deep history for both sides. The Green Bay Packers have not won at Gillette Stadium since 2002. Both teams have 18 playoff appearances since the NFL realigned in 2002. New England holds the league lead with 40 playoff wins, while Green Bay ranks third with 37. The two franchises have combined for 19 NFL championships. A New Era for the Patriots Brady’s return highlights how much the team has changed. He is no longer the quarterback on the field, and he does not run the offense from the sidelines. His statue stands outside the stadium, but the current roster has its own path. Former tight end Rob Gronkowski will be honored during halftime of the game. The broadcast will be the first time Brady calls a game for his former team. He has been back twice since retiring, once for his Hall of Fame induction and once for the statue unveiling. This Sunday, he brings a new perspective to the broadcast booth. On Sunday, Nov. 8, the Patriots will host the Packers, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m.

top.title: South Works Stadium Dream Is A Money Trap For Bears Fans
top.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Developer Curt Bailey is pushing hard to build the Chicago Bears stadium at the Old U.S. Steel South Works site on the South Side. He sees a skyline view and a boat ride to the venue as the perfect draw. But this flashy pitch ignores the cold hard math that drives NFL decisions. The team needs a deal that saves money, not one that adds billions in costs just to look good on a map. Bailey claims almost $1 billion of work is already happening there, including new university buildings and a hospital. “You can’t help but think this is where the Bears should be,” Bailey said, according to Yahoo Sports . That $1 billion figure sounds impressive until you look at who pays for it. The Bears are currently focused on Indiana because the state offered real tax breaks. Chicago politicians are now scrambling to write new laws to stop the team from leaving. Governor JB Pritzker says his office met with team leaders this week to get legislation ready for a vote in the veto session. “This is part of a continuing endeavor to try to make sure we have legislation ready to go for the veto session hearings on it the first week and a vote the second week of veto,” Pritzker said. The rush to keep the team in Illinois is a political move, not a business one. The Money Chaser Stadium expert Marc Ganis sees the real reason developers are circling the South Works site. They want profit, not football. For years, Ganis has observed that the Bears collaborated with the Arlington Heights government and have already cleared 300 acres of land there. “The fact that developers are starting to circle this tells me that they think there’s a chance it could happen because all they really want is to make money,” Ganis said. A private developer wants to cash in on the project, which means the Bears would lose control and likely pay more. The team already has the land in Arlington Heights ready to go without an intermediary asking for a cut. The Bears say they are still looking at two sites in Hammond, Indiana, while keeping the door open for Illinois options. The team stated they have a duty to look at every option available. “The Chicago Bears remain committed to building a world-class stadium and mixed-use district for our fans, the Chicagoland community and the team,” the Bears said in a statement on Friday, according to Yahoo Sports . But the core issue remains: Indiana offered a deal that works, and Illinois is trying to catch up with new laws. The South Works plan adds a layer of private financing that the Bears do not need. Stick to the Plan The Bears are coming off a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night to improve their record to 6-2. They face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next on Sunday night. The team has momentum and a young quarterback named Caleb Williams who has thrown just one interception this season.

top.title: Bayern, Dortmund win to stay tight at the top of Bundesliga
top.description: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha celebrates after scoring against Elversberg. (INA FASSBENDER) Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund remained neck and neck at the top of the German Bundesliga table after 2-1 wins over Mainz and Elversberg on Saturday. top.title: Tinubu to Nigerian youths: Your future depends on 2027 election
top.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian youths to collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate actively in the 2027 general elections, saying the outcome of the poll will have a direct bearing on their future. Tinubu made the call on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Addressing the youths at the rally, the president said the election should not be viewed as being about his personal ambition but about determining the future of the younger generation. “To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said. Tinubu urged Nigerians who were yet to collect their PVCs to do so, describing the voter card as the means through which citizens could determine the country’s leadership. “It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. “I take God, beg you,” he said. The president also identified economic development as a key tool for young Nigerians to overcome poverty, saying his administration was working to improve the economy and ensure that prosperity was widely shared. He said previous administrations had left behind unpaid pensions and gratuities running into billions and trillions of naira, adding that his government was clearing the outstanding obligations. “The people that governed before left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” Tinubu said. He listed retired professionals, including engineers, welders, and teachers, among those benefiting from the payments. “A retired engineer is receiving their gratuity right now. A retired welder is receiving the pension right now. A retired teacher is receiving the pension right now,” he added. nigeria.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
nigeria.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. nigeria.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
nigeria.description: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also hit with bans and fines, as was Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina’s coaching team. In a statement, AFA said FIFA’s appeals body had rejected their complaint against the sanctions handed out to Paredes and the association, but had reduced Molina’s punishment from a seven-match ban and $90,000 fine to four games and $60,000. nigeria.title: Hope you’ll visit 33 other states after Akwa Ibom ‘sleep’ – Obi tells Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to extend his visits to the remaining 33 states of the federation after spending a night in Akwa Ibom State. bi made the call in a post on X on Saturday, following Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom, where the president said his overnight stay would be a “second term presidential sleep” ahead of the 2027 election. Obi congratulated Tinubu on spending a night in a state outside Lagos and Abuja, urging the president to use such visits to engage directly with Nigerians and explain the impact of his administration. He said he hoped the Akwa Ibom visit would encourage Tinubu to travel to the other 33 states, spend time with the people and account for the resources accruing to the Federal Government. “I sincerely hope this visit will inspire you to travel to the remaining 33 states of the federation, spend time with the people and, more importantly, explain what your administration has done with the ₦15.8 trillion saved from the removal of fuel subsidy, the over $100 billion you have borrowed, the increased revenues accruing to the government from taxing Nigerians, and the additional government revenues which your administration celebrated last year as having surpassed its target,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor also demanded explanations on the impact of government policies on poverty, education, healthcare and electricity. He asked the President to state how many Nigerians had been lifted out of poverty, how many out-of-school children had returned to school and how many functional primary healthcare centres had been built. Obi also questioned the improvement in electricity supply, recalling Tinubu’s earlier promise that Nigerians should not vote for him if his administration failed to fix the power sector. On insecurity, he said Nigerians deserved an explanation of what the government had done to secure the country, which he noted still ranks among the world’s most terrorised countries. “Mr President, Nigerians deserve answers. They deserve to know what has been done with the resources entrusted to your government,” Obi said. He added that the New Nigeria he seeks to build would be founded on accountability, transparency and the measurable impact of public resources on citizens. Tinubu had on Friday told supporters at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom, describing it as a “second term presidential sleep” and expressing confidence in securing re-election in 2027. nigeria.title: Oyo’ll no longer depend on oil, raw materials for economic prosperity – Makinde
nigeria.description: …state targets global market for arts, crafts By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has declared its determination to move beyond dependence on conventional sources of revenue by harnessing the economic potential of arts, crafts, cultural festivals, and tourism to generate foreign exchange, attract international investments, and create employment opportunities. The government said it was working to transform Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage into commercially viable products for the global export market, positioning the creative economy as a major driver of economic growth and sustainable development. The initiative, which sought to unlock the enormous economic value of indigenous artistic expressions, traditional knowledge, and cultural assets, will be driven through the Oyo State Business Forum 2026, with the theme “Investment and Export Promotion of Arts and Crafts Business in Oyo State.” The forum is expected to bring together investors, artists, craftsmen, exporters, policymakers, and development partners to explore investment opportunities, strengthen export capacity, and expand the international market for Nigerian arts and crafts. Speaking at a press briefing to announce the forum, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dr. Wasiu Olatubosun, said the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde was deliberately repositioning culture beyond its traditional function as a custodian of heritage to become a productive economic sector capable of generating wealth, attracting investments, and contributing meaningfully to national development. Olatubosun, who spoke at the briefing organized in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment and Public-Private Partnership Agency (OYSIPA) at the state Secretariat, Ibadan, described Nigeria’s cultural wealth as an enormous but largely untapped economic resource that could compete favorably in the international marketplace. He maintained that traditional festivals, indigenous knowledge, artistic expressions, and locally produced crafts possessed considerable commercial value and could become major export commodities if properly researched, documented, developed, and marketed. According to him, the state government is also repositioning its cultural festivals from routine annual celebrations into internationally competitive tourism and entertainment products capable of attracting foreign visitors, investors, and members of the African diaspora. He identified the recent inscription of the Sango Festival on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a major boost to Oyo State’s international cultural standing and an opportunity to attract greater global attention. The commissioner explained that the recognition had taken the annual festival in Oyo Town beyond its traditional geographical and cultural boundaries, making it an increasingly attractive destination for international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, and media organizations from Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

nigeria.title: Tinubu-Shettima ticket most formidable in Nigeria’s history, says APC chair
nigeria.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the most formidable in Nigeria’s political history, urging Nigerians to support their re-election in 2027. Yilwatda said Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate the economic reforms and infrastructure projects initiated by his administration. He made the remarks on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition Presidential Campaign Rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said the Tinubu-Shettima ticket combined political experience, courage and leadership capacity needed to address the country’s challenges. “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country. He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria,” he said. Yilwatda defended the administration’s economic policies, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, describing them as necessary steps towards rebuilding the economy and strengthening public finances. Although he acknowledged that the reforms had created difficulties for households and businesses, he said the government was working to cushion their effects through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions and infrastructure investments. The APC chairman also praised Tinubu’s infrastructure programme, particularly major highway projects, which he said would improve connectivity, facilitate trade and create economic opportunities. “We have a President who understands that development cannot happen without infrastructure. He has initiated an ambitious infrastructure revolution through major highway projects that will connect different parts of Nigeria, open up economic corridors, facilitate the movement of goods and services and create new opportunities for our people,” Yilwatda said. nigeria.title: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat
nigeria.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has said United States President Donald Trump deserved to be defeated in the midterm elections, describing the setback as “entirely self-inflicted.” In an interview with The Independent , Badenoch criticised Trump’s handling of the Iran war, his trade policies and his treatment of allies. She said his approach did not reflect conservative principles. The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major blow to Trump’s Republican Party. Asked whether Trump deserved the defeat, Badenoch replied: “Yeah. He has not been acting in the way that I would consider conservative.” She condemned his tariffs, threats towards Canada and Greenland, and disputes with allies, saying they contradicted the conservative emphasis on free markets and better trade. “Where is the push for free markets and better trade… rather than protectionism, America first, the squabbling with allies? That’s not what conservatives do,” she said. Badenoch also criticised Trump’s personal attacks on journalists and political figures, stating that his conduct fell short of the standards expected of a statesman. “Trump is very charming in person, but you see the way that he talks about journalists, about individuals. It doesn’t meet the standards a statesman should meet – always wanting to get dirty in terms of insults and so on,” she said. She expressed particular unhappiness with Trump’s remarks about British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and described his treatment of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House as “awful.” On the Iran conflict, Badenoch said she understood and supported Trump’s initial decision to take military action due to concerns about Iran acquiring nuclear weapons, but questioned the lack of a clear strategy. “We don’t want them getting nuclear weapons. But where’s the plan?” she asked. Badenoch added that she would have been content if Trump had lost the 2024 presidential election to Kamala Harris. When asked which of the two candidates she preferred, she said: “I would say I like them both equally. Make of that what you will.” She further argued that Trump had squandered the broad coalition of voters that helped him win the presidency, including increased support from Latino and Black voters. “What’s the first thing he does? Tariffs, and then talking about Greenland and Canada. A lot of people were wondering, ‘What are you doing?’” she said. Badenoch became leader of the UK Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in November 2024. Born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in London in 1980 to Nigerian parents, she previously served as Business and Trade Secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. nigeria.title: Okafor strike for Leeds ends Tottenham’s winning run
nigeria.description: Leeds rode their luck to beat in-form Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, benefiting from a controversial decision to allow Jayden Bogle to stay on the pitch after an ugly tackle on Mathys Tel. Substitute Noah Okafor was the match-winner, making an almost immediate impact after being introduced by Leeds boss Daniel Farke in the 77th minute. The home team started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area. As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium. Leeds got the benefit of a contentious decision about 10 minutes before the break when Bogle caught Tel’s trailing ankle with his studs, leaving the Tottenham winger writhing on the ground in pain. After a lengthy VAR check no action was taken against Bogle, who was not even booked for the challenge, but Tel was forced off a few minutes later, hobbling off to be replaced by Dominic Solanke. Leeds had two big chances early in the second half as Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header was blocked by Solanke before Nico Elvedi nodded wide on the follow-up. Calvert-Lewin then burst forward again but opted to pass to Ao Tanaka rather than shooting and the Japanese international skied his shot. Leeds were now on the front foot and Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful stop after Sean Longstaff’s swivel and shot. But they got the goal their pressure deserved in the 79th minute. Harry Wilson, another substitute, controlled the ball and played it into the path of Okafor, who gave Kinsky no chance. Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser but goalkeeper James Trafford made a brilliant save from Jan Paul van Hecke’s header. The result ends Tottenham’s run of three straight league wins while it was the first victory in six games for Leeds, who climbed to eighth in the table. nigeria.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. sports.title: Jared McCain rediscovers outside jumper in OKC's win over Grizzlies
sports.description: On a pair of catch-and-shoot looks, Jared McCain rediscovered his groove. His undermanned squad quickly put up a double-digit lead. They can thank their en-fuego-style outside shooting for that. After a cold spell, the 22-year-old showed what the positive side of his shooting variance can look like. The Oklahoma City Thunder looked their best since Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) started with a 124-97 win over the Memphis Grizzlies . The butt-whooping was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B stage. McCain finished with 21 points on 9-of-14 shooting and five rebounds. He shot 3-of-8 from 3. He also had four steals and one block. Do you think McCain heard Bennett Stirtz's footsteps coming for his playing time? He's certainly played like somebody with a fire lit underneath his seat. Showing an inkling of confidence, the microwave scorer was hot throughout the night. Sure, the outside jumpers fell. But his scoring attack within the paint has also been a nice surprise so far. "Getting those transition shots where you got to guard Ajay, me or Shai, them driving to the basket is awesome for us," McCain said. "They make great decisions. For us, we just continue that. At halftime, we just kept our foot on the pedal." McCain had 12 points in the first quarter. He helped the Thunder get away from this one early. As Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gladly took a backseat after back-to-back 40-point nights, it was he and Ajay Mitchell who delivered OKC's first lethal punch to Memphis. sports.title: Tom Brady Returns To Broadcast Patriots Game Sunday
sports.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The legend walks back into Gillette Stadium, but not as the man who threw the passes, according to Sports Illustrated . Tom Brady will serve as a broadcaster for the first time on Sunday, calling the Patriots game against the Green Bay Packers. This marks a major shift for the seven-time Super Bowl champion, who has skipped calling his old team since joining FOX Sports in 2024. The network finally puts him in the booth for this matchup, ending a long dry spell of him avoiding New England on air. Brady told FOX’s Colin Cowherd that the moment feels heavy. This week, Brady told FOX’s Colin Cowherd, “It’ll certainly be emotional,” and he plans to focus on the team’s culture rather than his own past glory. The plan is to show fans how the program works right now. This approach fits a team that has moved past the dynasty years and is building something new under coach Mike Vrabel. Vrabel Keeps It Light Head coach Mike Vrabel took a different view when asked about his former teammate. He played eight years with Brady and won three Super Bowls together. Instead of getting emotional, Vrabel joked that he would handle their catch-up over a video call. He noted that he expects to see Brady in person soon at Rob Gronkowski’s Hall of Fame induction on Saturday. The banter shows a comfortable relationship between the two men. Vrabel knows the history, but he is focused on the present season. The Patriots are 5-3 and looking to build momentum after a win in Miami. Weather and Rivalry History The game faces a different kind of pressure from the sky. Apple Weather projects an 80% chance of rain for the area on Sunday. Fans should bring a jacket as temperatures drop into the upper 40s by the end of the game. This matchup also carries deep history for both sides. The Green Bay Packers have not won at Gillette Stadium since 2002. Both teams have 18 playoff appearances since the NFL realigned in 2002. New England holds the league lead with 40 playoff wins, while Green Bay ranks third with 37. The two franchises have combined for 19 NFL championships. A New Era for the Patriots Brady’s return highlights how much the team has changed. He is no longer the quarterback on the field, and he does not run the offense from the sidelines. His statue stands outside the stadium, but the current roster has its own path. Former tight end Rob Gronkowski will be honored during halftime of the game. sports.title: South Works Stadium Dream Is A Money Trap For Bears Fans
sports.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Developer Curt Bailey is pushing hard to build the Chicago Bears stadium at the Old U.S. Steel South Works site on the South Side. He sees a skyline view and a boat ride to the venue as the perfect draw. But this flashy pitch ignores the cold hard math that drives NFL decisions. The team needs a deal that saves money, not one that adds billions in costs just to look good on a map. Bailey claims almost $1 billion of work is already happening there, including new university buildings and a hospital. “You can’t help but think this is where the Bears should be,” Bailey said, according to Yahoo Sports . That $1 billion figure sounds impressive until you look at who pays for it. The Bears are currently focused on Indiana because the state offered real tax breaks. Chicago politicians are now scrambling to write new laws to stop the team from leaving. Governor JB Pritzker says his office met with team leaders this week to get legislation ready for a vote in the veto session. “This is part of a continuing endeavor to try to make sure we have legislation ready to go for the veto session hearings on it the first week and a vote the second week of veto,” Pritzker said. The rush to keep the team in Illinois is a political move, not a business one. The Money Chaser Stadium expert Marc Ganis sees the real reason developers are circling the South Works site. They want profit, not football. For years, Ganis has observed that the Bears collaborated with the Arlington Heights government and have already cleared 300 acres of land there. “The fact that developers are starting to circle this tells me that they think there’s a chance it could happen because all they really want is to make money,” Ganis said. A private developer wants to cash in on the project, which means the Bears would lose control and likely pay more. The team already has the land in Arlington Heights ready to go without an intermediary asking for a cut. The Bears say they are still looking at two sites in Hammond, Indiana, while keeping the door open for Illinois options. The team stated they have a duty to look at every option available. “The Chicago Bears remain committed to building a world-class stadium and mixed-use district for our fans, the Chicagoland community and the team,” the Bears said in a statement on Friday, according to Yahoo Sports . But the core issue remains: Indiana offered a deal that works, and Illinois is trying to catch up with new laws. The South Works plan adds a layer of private financing that the Bears do not need. Stick to the Plan The Bears are coming off a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night to improve their record to 6-2. They face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next on Sunday night. The team has momentum and a young quarterback named Caleb Williams who has thrown just one interception this season.

sports.title: Rob Gronkowski’s GOAT Tight End Case: How Patriots Legend Set Standard at Position

Rob Gronkowski's legacy continues to linger on gridirons across the country five years after his swansong. The former Patriots and Buccaneers standout was, at his pinnacle, football's greatest tight end, a devastating blend of speed, size and precision who gashed more than a few secondaries across his 11 seasons in the top-flight. Five years after his retirement, Gronkowski's impact continues to loom. So much so, in fact, that some feels he's not only the greatest tight end they have ever laid eyes on; he might be the greatest to ever play the sport. With that, NESN examines Gronkowski's legacy, incluing whether he can truly be considered football's greatest-ever tight end. Rob Gronkowski’s GOAT Tight End Case There is ample statistical evidence that Gronkowski is the greatest tight end in NFL history. While Gronkowski "only" ranks sixth all-time in receiving yards and 11th all-time in receptions among tight ends, he places third in yards per game among tight ends to start at least 50 games, trailing only Travis Kelce and Pete Retzlaff, per Stathead . He recorded 92 touchdowns in his career, the third-highest mark in league history. However, the two players in front of him — Antonio Gates (116) and Tony Gonzalez (111) played 62 and 126 more games than Gronkowski did, respectively. His 9.7 yard per target mark ranks second among tight ends, one yard greater than that of Kelce. He also boasts more the joint second-most first-team All-Pro selections for a tight end (four), tying Kelce, Dave Casper and Shannon Sharpe in the mark. He accomplished that feat in fewer games than his counterpart. With nearly a handful of Super Bowl rings — three with the Patriots, one with the Buccaneers — Gronkowski also proved his worth when the lights were brightest. He ranks second all-time in catches (98), receiving yards (1,389) and receiving touchdowns (15) in the postseason, trailing only Kelce. To be sure, Gronkowski isn't the only candidate for the title of football's greatest-ever tight end. Kelce has an equally compelling case. Perhaps the Chiefs standout makes up for his slight disadvantage in Super Bowls (for now) by posting gaudy numbers over a longer period of his career. Other notable talents who can reasonably challenge for the throne include Gonzalez, Gates and Sharpe. Nevertheless, Gronkowski is arguably in pole position for the crown. That will suit him — and New England supporters — just fine. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also have grid penalties, 10 places for Leclerc and five for Russell. Hamilton initially had only a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season, but the new internal combustion engine that was fitted on Saturday morning failed in final practice. That meant Ferrari decided to fit an entire new power-unit to his car, hence the bigger penalty. Verstappen had an all-new engine fitted after Red Bull discovered problems after Friday practice. Leclerc and Russell have both fitted new internal combustion engines. The penalty for Leclerc is bigger than Russell's because it is the first time Ferrari have exceeded the limit of four engines per season on his car, while Russell had already gone beyond that. Verstappen famously won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from 17th on the grid after an engine penalty in a wet race. Qualifying is set to be wet, after rain started about an hour before the session, and it is expected to continue overnight, with forecasts saying it could rain at any point on race day. Meanwhile, F1 announced on Saturday that Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit had extended its contract to host a grand prix until 2035. F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "Brazil is an important part of F1's history and our future, and I am delighted that this five-year extension will see us continue racing in Sao Paulo until 2035. "The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary, and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo. "The continued success and excitement surrounding the event shows why it holds such a special place on our calendar, and this agreement underlines our long-term commitment to Brazil." Ferguson told The Register in an interview that while Fireworks AI, a managed inference provider, supports on-prem AI, "we're trying to push people more and more away from it because frankly, it's just the economics." The GPU hardware is just so expensive that if you can't keep it fully utilized, it's a waste of money, he contends. Ten thousand GPUs, he said, represent a billion dollars of capital. "You don't want those things to be sitting idle," he said. For companies with particularly sensitive workloads, Ferguson said, Fireworks is happy to work something out – it offers a service called Sovereign for just that purpose and it has partners like Microsoft that can help. But most inference work probably doesn't need that level of protection, he said. "The state of the art for everyone is to have a portfolio of models," he explained. "In fact, I think most people don't know that the best model in the world's not Astra. The best model in the world's not Fable. The best model is literally a portfolio and we can prove it. You are always better routing between a few models than to do one singular model." That's what Fireworks does through Nexus and its API, alongside competitors like Together AI, Baseten, and DeepInfra. As a managed inference platform, Fireworks AI routes inference tasks to whichever model, frontier model subscription, or API is best suited to handle them. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land.
